evidence.excerpt:
Memory has become a central mechanism for extending large language models
(LLMs) beyond fixed context windows, stateless interaction, and static paramet-
ric knowledge. This survey organizes the literature around three complementary
dimensions: the life cycle of memory, the storage substrate, and the system
role that memory plays in LLM-based agents, while using cognitive-science-
inspired memory concepts as a lightweight conceptual motivation rather than
as a separate technical contribution or implementation family. On this basis, we
distinguish three mechanism families: nonparametric memory, where information
is stored outside model parameters in text, graph, multimodal, or database-like
structures; parametric memory, where information is stored or accessed through
activations, key-value caches, learned modules, adapter-based parameterizations,
or model weights; and memory for agent

ory analogies, and benchmarks that test memory persistence or long-horizon behavior.
A method is included when memory is central to the mechanism or evaluation claim,
not merely an incidental implementation detail. We exclude methods that only perform
one-off retrieval, prompt compression, or long-context inference unless they directly
address memory persistence, lifecycle management, update behavior, or memory-
guided future action. This scope makes the paper a mechanism-centered survey rather
than a general survey of RAG, long-context modeling, or agent frameworks.

evidence.excerpt:
Memory overlaps with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and long-context mod-
eling, but it is not identical to either. RAG is primarily retrieval-centered: the original
RAG formulation retrieves Wikipedia passages from a dense vector index with a
neural retriever, while later RAG-style systems may use sparse, dense, or hybrid
3
retrieval (Lewis et al. 2020; Karpukhin et al. 2020). Long-context modeling is capacity-
centered: the system attempts to process more tokens within a single inference context.
Memory is lifecycle-centered: it requires decisions about what to store, how to rep-
resent it, when to update it, how to resolve conflicts, how to delete it, and how to
evaluate whether it improves future behavior. This distinction is important because
a system may have a long context window or a retriever without having reliable
long-term memory.

Long-term systems fail when they write too much, write too little, or write incorrect
abstractions. Better memory construction should distinguish durable facts, transient
preferences, temporary task states, and uncertain observations. It should also support
explicit contradiction handling and confidence-aware revision. Future research should
23
move beyond heuristic summarization toward write policies that are evaluated against
delayed downstream tasks, not only immediate extraction quality.

evidence.excerpt:
Long-term memory often contains personal, proprietary, or task-sensitive informa-
tion. Multi-user, multi-agent, and edge–cloud settings require access control, prove-
nance tracking, permission-aware retrieval, conflict management, secure deletion, and
privacy-preserving personalized memory management (Chen et al. 2026c). Paramet-
ric memory is especially challenging because a single remembered fact may not be
directly inspectable or removable. Practical memory systems should therefore expose
deletion logs, memory scopes, user consent controls, and policy-aware retrieval filters.
24
These governance mechanisms should be treated as core technical components rather
than deployment afterthoughts.

evidence.excerpt:
Current benchmarks cover long-context retrieval, conversational memory, multimodal
understanding, and simulation environments, but evaluation remains fragmented.
Future benchmarks should measure memory write quality, update correctness, absten-
tion, hallucinated memory use, privacy leakage, temporal consistency, and downstream
task success. They should also distinguish between genuine memory use and success
through long-context pattern matching. One practical approach is to evaluate agents
under controlled memory ablations, where memory contents are removed, corrupted,
delayed, or replaced to test whether the model truly depends on the intended memory
mechanism.

Memory research for LLMs has moved from simple retrieval augmentation toward a
diverse ecosystem of nonparametric stores, graph memories, multimodal memories,
parametric memory modules, and self-evolving agent systems. This survey organized
the literature around a lightweight cognitive-science-inspired conceptual motivation
layer, three computational mechanism families—nonparametric memory, parametric
memory, and memory for agent evolution—and a cross-cutting evaluation layer that
tests whether these mechanisms produce durable benefits. Across these families, the
central design questions are how to construct memory, how to manage and consolidate

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No optimization-to-evaluation loop exists because the work is a structured review paper without experimental model evaluation [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Not applicable; the manuscript reports no empirical benchmarking of a newly proposed model, instead validating its contribution through literature coverage and comparative conceptual analysis [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; the manuscript is a qualitative literature survey and taxonomy rather than a system optimized against any training, tuning, or selection signal [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The analytical claims, conceptual boundaries, and distinctions from general RAG/long-context methods align well with the detailed literature breakdown and synthesis provided [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0008, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0012, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0098].
primary.evaluation_assessment: As a comprehensive review paper, it validates its categorization by systematically mapping a broad literature base into comparative tables, detailing trade-offs, metrics, and evaluation benchmarks across plain-text, multimodal, and simulation environments [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0021, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0084, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0088].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No experimental evaluation is conducted as the manuscript is a structured review paper [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Not applicable; the manuscript provides comparative conceptual analysis and literature classification without empirical benchmarking of a newly proposed model [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; this work is a qualitative literature survey and taxonomy rather than an optimized model or algorithm [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].

primary.limitations: The manuscript explicitly discusses current gaps across memory architectures, including challenges in reliable memory writing, privacy, deletion/governance, error amplification, and fragmented benchmark evaluation [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0088, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0091, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0095, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0097].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology defines clear selection criteria using keyword search and citation tracing across peer-reviewed and preprint venues, explicitly scoping inclusion around systems treating memory as an explicit design object rather than incidental scaling [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0010, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0011]. The proposed taxonomy rigorously compares mechanisms using recurring lifecycle questions [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0024, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0026].
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-scoped survey that establishes clear conceptual taxonomies and lifecycle-oriented analytical tools for LLM memory systems without overclaiming empirical findings beyond its scope as a literature synthesis [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0008, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].
primary.scoped_contribution: A structured survey and alignment framework organizing LLM memory literature across five dimensions (conceptual motivation, memory lifecycle, storage substrate, system role, and evaluation), classifying methods into nonparametric, parametric, and agent-evolution memory mechanisms [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0002, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0008, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0021].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-scoped survey that establishes clear conceptual taxonomies and lifecycle-oriented analytical tools for LLM memory systems without overclaiming empirical findings beyond its scope as a literature synthesis [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0008, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0100].
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript explicitly discusses current gaps across memory architectures, including challenges in reliable memory writing, privacy, deletion/governance, error amplification, and fragmented benchmark evaluation [E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0088, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0091, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0095, E5a9e96da6f3f1244-B0097].
